name: Improve the solution
decision: what can I change to improve my solution?
description: Choose the next concrete intervention using the available evidence, then revisit the tree after measuring its effect.

children.name: Improve the evidence for choosing changes
children.decision: Which uncertainty should I resolve before another performance change?
children.description: Choose the next measurement or comparison when existing scores cannot reliably guide improvement.

children.name: Choose a validation design
children.decision: Which split design should I test for this data?
children.description: Select the split constraint that best represents the intended unseen examples.

children.name: Preserve target proportions
children.description: Use stratified folds, binning a continuous target when needed, to stabilize target distributions.

children.name: Hold related examples together
children.description: Use entity, source, topic, or defensible inferred groups to keep related examples out of opposing folds.

children.name: Probe subgroup allocation
children.description: Compare subgroup allocation schemes with a separate disjoint evaluation set; overlapping train and validation rows in the source trajectories do not provide an unbiased score.

children.name: Change holdout allocation
children.description: Compare holdout fractions or cross-validation against full-data fitting while preserving an independent selection signal.

children.name: Choose a trustworthy comparison
children.decision: Which measurement would resolve the uncertainty in the apparent gain?
children.description: Distinguish score noise, misleading validation, confounded edits, and incorrect metric computation.

children.name: Measure repeat-run variability
children.description: Repeat an unchanged configuration with pinned artifacts and compare score distributions rather than single best runs.

children.name: Check local and external score agreement
children.description: Compare local validation with earlier external evaluations and use local selection when leaderboard resolution or sample size is inadequate.

children.name: Isolate one change
children.description: Compare configurations differing in one meaningful factor, or use a small factorial comparison for an interaction.

children.name: Align the evaluation callback
children.description: Implement and verify the task metric and its optimization direction in validation and early stopping.

children.name: Inspect data structure
children.description: Inspect entity counts, ordering, feature types, missingness, and target distributions before selecting a representation.

children.name: Choose a response to an unsuccessful search
children.decision: Should I restore, narrow, or redirect the current experiment?
children.description: Use the size and attribution of regressions to choose the next experiment.

children.name: Restore the proven configuration
children.description: Recover the exact known-good configuration before reintroducing changes separately.

children.name: Move to a different improvement lever
children.description: Stop a saturated local sweep and test a qualitatively different source of signal or modeling change.

children.name: Narrow the parameter search
children.description: Bracket a promising continuous parameter range and refine it with controlled local comparisons.

children.name: Establish a working baseline
children.description: Build and evaluate a minimal end-to-end solution before adding further complexity.

children.name: Test a coordinated bundle
children.description: Compare a jointly changed configuration with a saved baseline when the changes are coupled, then ablate the bundle before attributing its gain.

children.name: Repair incorrect or mismatched predictions
children.decision: Which failure mechanism should I investigate first?
children.description: Choose a correctness repair when predictions, scores, or execution contradict the intended pipeline.

children.name: Restore model and input compatibility
children.decision: Which training-to-inference contract is broken?
children.description: Match artifacts and transformations to the configuration that produced the learned weights.

children.name: Match architecture and weights
children.description: Reconstruct the trained architecture and inspect strict checkpoint loading, tensor dimensions, and missing or prefixed state keys.

children.name: Match input preprocessing
children.description: Restore the training-time resolution, filtering, normalization, feature extraction, and input format at inference.

children.name: Match tokenizer and vocabulary
children.description: Use the training tokenizer, special-token definitions, vocabulary size, and token-index logic with the checkpoint.

children.name: Match feature schema and encoders
children.description: Reuse fitted encoders and the exact feature names, ordering, and dimensions expected by the downstream model.

children.name: Locate a data-flow defect
children.decision: Where should I check for lost or corrupted signal?
children.description: Trace data and predictions through the stage most consistent with the observed failure.

children.name: Restore row and identifier alignment
children.description: Join auxiliary features and prediction files by explicit identifiers and reverse any sorting before output.

children.name: Restore missing model contributions
children.description: Verify every intended fold, branch, and model executes and contributes the intended prediction array.

children.name: Correct aggregation arithmetic
children.description: Check numeric array types, axes, divisors, group normalization, weights, and shapes in ensemble calculations.

children.name: Trace inputs and prediction signal
children.description: Inspect small examples, stage outputs, variance, and data sources to locate placeholders, constant predictions, or wrong inputs.

children.name: Repair invalid numerical values
children.description: Check inputs and intermediate tensors for NaNs or infinities and apply model-appropriate handling.

children.name: Correct the custom objective implementation
children.description: Audit custom-loss gradients, Hessians, shapes, and callback inputs before attributing a score collapse to modeling.

children.name: Resolve the first execution failure
children.decision: What dependency failure prevents the intended computation?
children.description: Repair the concrete failing contract before running a full experiment.

children.name: Resolve artifact paths
children.description: List available artifacts and fix checkpoint, configuration, and preprocessing paths before loading.

children.name: Resolve package compatibility
children.description: Correct imports, offline dependencies, versions, and module search paths to load the intended implementation.

children.name: Match computation devices
children.description: Align model and tensor devices or use a supported CPU backend before re-enabling acceleration.

children.name: Repair syntax or API contracts
children.description: Use a minimal failing example to correct variable scope, parameter names, dataframe semantics, or function signatures.

children.name: Write the intended submission
children.description: Validate output columns, row count, final prediction variable, filename, and file-writing execution.

children.name: Change the information presented to the model
children.decision: Which input representation should I change next?
children.description: Choose a concrete feature or preprocessing experiment based on missing signal or excess noise.

children.name: Represent repeated or structured records
children.decision: Which structured feature construction should I test?
children.description: Choose a representation that captures the kind of information missing from the current features.

children.name: Add entity-level summary statistics
children.description: Aggregate repeated records with controlled additions of location, spread, extrema, counts, or last values.

children.name: Add temporal changes or recent windows
children.description: Compute lags, first-to-last changes, or recent-window statistics to represent temporal dynamics.

children.name: Add domain interactions
children.description: Construct semantically justified differences, ratios, products, or composite features and test their marginal value.

children.name: Change numeric precision or scaling
children.description: Compare rounding, precision, or scaling choices without changing the underlying observations.

children.name: Change missing-value handling
children.description: Compare native missing-value support with explicit model-appropriate imputation.

children.name: Add structured metadata
children.description: Encode relevant source, category, time, or other available metadata as features.

children.name: Represent text for the model
children.decision: Which text representation should I test next?
children.description: Select the representation whose information is absent or poorly captured in the current pipeline.

children.name: Change text normalization
children.description: Compare minimal tokenizer-compatible processing with domain-specific cleaning, cropping, or spelling normalization.

children.name: Change text input structure
children.description: Test metadata prompts, paired inputs, separate text streams, or explicit formatting with matching training support.

children.name: Tune sparse n-gram features
children.description: Compare word and character n-grams, frequency cutoffs, and vocabulary ranges.

children.name: Add linguistic or structural statistics
children.description: Extract text counts, readability, syntax, sentiment, or section and sentence summaries as candidate features.

children.name: Add pretrained dense representations
children.description: Extract pooled pretrained embeddings or low-dimensional semantic representations and validate their added signal.

children.name: Add similarity or auxiliary-task features
children.description: Use training-neighbor labels or predictions from related-data models as carefully aligned auxiliary features.

children.name: Represent images and signals
children.decision: Which spatial or signal representation should I test?
children.description: Choose a representation change that addresses lost detail, unwanted variation, or missing channels.

children.name: Sweep input resolution
children.description: Compare nearby input resolutions with compatible checkpoints while holding other model settings fixed.

children.name: Change time-frequency resolution
children.description: Compare spectral transforms, window sizes, hop lengths, or frequency bands using compatible training and inference.

children.name: Change the observed window
children.description: Test spatial crops or temporal context windows against the label scope and training configuration.

children.name: Change signal filtering or clipping
children.description: Compare justified filtering, noise suppression, clipping, or sampling settings and validate their consistency with training.

children.name: Change input normalization
children.description: Compare channel or instance normalization and dynamic-range transforms using training-supported settings.

children.name: Change channel layout or rendering
children.description: Test added channels, pseudo-image shapes, or color representations while preserving sample and channel identity.

children.name: Control the feature set
children.decision: Which feature-set reduction or refresh should I perform?
children.description: Choose how to remove noise or repair stale selection without silently excluding new useful features.

children.name: Ablate a feature family
children.description: Remove or restore one candidate feature group and measure its incremental contribution.

children.name: Estimate feature relevance
children.description: Aggregate importance estimates across folds or compare importance methods before choosing a subset.

children.name: Tune the retained feature count
children.description: Sweep feature-selection thresholds or count limits against held-out performance.

children.name: Recompute feature selection
children.description: Regenerate and version the selected feature list whenever the candidate feature space changes.

children.name: Reduce dense representation dimensions
children.description: Prune embedding sources or dimensions when expanded dense features introduce noise or exceed resources.

children.name: Change training examples or targets
children.decision: Which data or target intervention should I test?
children.description: Choose a change to supervision or sample exposure based on noise, imbalance, censoring, or distribution shift.

children.name: Choose training examples
children.decision: Which change to the training population is justified?
children.description: Compare data additions, removals, and reweighting according to their likely relevance to unseen examples.

children.name: Filter or deduplicate training data
children.description: Test removing noisy, redundant, overlapping, or distribution-mismatched samples against an unchanged validation set.

children.name: Add labeled auxiliary data
children.description: Integrate relevant external labeled examples and compare joint versus staged use.

children.name: Use pseudo-labeled examples
children.description: Evaluate models trained with unlabeled-data pseudo-labels against supervised counterparts.

children.name: Reweight or resample subpopulations
children.description: Change class or source exposure through appropriate sample weights or resampling.

children.name: Interpolate training examples
children.description: Test synthetic within-class neighbors or mixup-style feature interpolation and ablate it if harmful.

children.name: Choose a target formulation
children.decision: Which supervision representation should I test?
children.description: Select a target formulation that reflects censoring, ordering, or group-specific evaluation.

children.name: Transform censored outcomes
children.description: Compare regression-friendly survival probabilities, hazards, or rank-based targets with consistent risk direction.

children.name: Construct targets within evaluation groups
children.description: Estimate target transforms separately within the groups used by the evaluation criterion.

children.name: Tune target centering or transformation strength
children.description: Sweep target offsets, nonlinear strength parameters, or centering conventions while preserving inverse transforms.

children.name: Use ordinal or classification supervision
children.description: Compare regression with ordinal cumulative outputs or multiclass supervision for discrete ordered labels.

children.name: Choose training augmentation
children.decision: Which augmentation should I test against the unaugmented baseline?
children.description: Choose perturbations consistent with label invariances and observed overfitting.

children.name: Use mild image perturbations
children.description: Compare controlled brightness, contrast, or geometric augmentation strengths and remove harmful additions.

children.name: Mask signal regions
children.description: Test random time-frequency masking to reduce reliance on particular signal regions.

children.name: Mix labeled examples
children.description: Compare standard and multi-example mixup with label mixing appropriate to the task.

children.name: Change the learned model
children.decision: Which model-fitting change is the most plausible next intervention?
children.description: Choose an architecture, objective, or optimization experiment based on observed fit limitations.

children.name: Choose a model family or initialization
children.decision: Which replacement model should I test as a standalone candidate?
children.description: Compare alternatives while preserving data, validation, and inference correctness.

children.name: Change pretrained backbone or capacity
children.description: Compare backbone families or sizes with their matching tokenizer, head dimensions, and trained checkpoints.

children.name: Use domain-adapted pretraining
children.description: Test pretrained weights adapted to the task domain against a general-pretraining baseline.

children.name: Change tree learner or boosting variant
children.description: Compare tree libraries, standard versus dropout boosting, or equivalent model implementations on the same features.

children.name: Fit a model for a different representation
children.description: Build a standalone model suited to raw signals, spectral inputs, fixed embeddings, or another complementary representation.

children.name: Change the prediction architecture
children.decision: Which architectural component should I alter?
children.description: Target the representational bottleneck while retaining compatibility between learned weights and inference code.

children.name: Change head capacity or attention
children.description: Compare shared versus separate heads, hidden layers, and attention blocks on a fixed backbone.

children.name: Change pooling or representation normalization
children.description: Compare sequence or hidden-layer pooling and normalization before the prediction layer.

children.name: Add auxiliary supervision
children.description: Train a parallel classification or summary head and compare its effect on the main prediction.

children.name: Change feature-level modality fusion
children.description: Compare separate input branches, concatenation, and averaging using a correspondingly trained prediction head.

children.name: Change training-time dropout
children.description: Tune head dropout or multisample dropout to control variance during fitting.

children.name: Tune a tree learner
children.decision: Which tree-fitting constraint should I adjust?
children.description: Choose the parameter family indicated by underfitting, overfitting, or incomplete optimization.

children.name: Tune tree depth and leaves
children.description: Sweep depth and leaf limits to balance representational capacity and generalization.

children.name: Tune penalties and subsampling
children.description: Compare leaf penalties and row or column sampling while fixing other capacity settings.

children.name: Coordinate boosting rate and rounds
children.description: Adjust learning rate together with sufficient boosting rounds and verify convergence.

children.name: Change stopping patience or criterion
children.description: Compare stopping patience, monitored validation sets, and fixed-round training using observed learning curves.

children.name: Reset uncertain tree parameters
children.description: Compare an extensively hand-tuned configuration with a controlled library-default baseline.

children.name: Tune neural optimization or loss
children.decision: Which training change should I test?
children.description: Use convergence and objective mismatch to choose an optimization intervention.

children.name: Tune learning rate
children.description: Bracket the fine-tuning learning rate while checking convergence and instability.

children.name: Change optimizer or learning-rate schedule
children.description: Compare optimizer or decay schedule choices under a matched training budget.

children.name: Change training duration or stages
children.description: Compare epoch budgets, staged fine-tuning, or batch size using held-out learning behavior.

children.name: Change the training objective
children.description: Compare metric-aligned losses or custom objective shapes against the standard objective.

children.name: Make component training cross-validated
children.description: Train and persist a component on consistent folds with valid held-out predictions and data loaders.

children.name: Change the prediction pool
children.decision: How should I change which trained predictors contribute?
children.description: Choose a candidate addition, replacement, reduction, or repetition before tuning the blend.

children.name: Choose the source of ensemble diversity
children.decision: What kind of additional predictor should I test?
children.description: Add one source whose errors may complement the current pool and verify its marginal contribution.

children.name: Add a different model family
children.description: Add predictions from a distinct architecture or algorithm family and test them alongside the intact baseline.

children.name: Add an alternative input representation
children.description: Add a model trained with a different modality, preprocessing, feature set, or input window.

children.name: Add an alternative supervision recipe
children.description: Add models trained with different target transformations or complementary training recipes.

children.name: Average more fold or snapshot predictions
children.description: Compare incremental fold or checkpoint averaging with the current single or smaller predictor pool.

children.name: Average independently seeded models
children.description: Train or load independent seed checkpoints and measure the marginal value of additional runs.

children.name: Average checkpoint weights
children.description: Test stochastic weight averaging of compatible checkpoints before inference.

children.name: Choose ensemble membership
children.decision: Which membership experiment should I run next?
children.description: Use standalone and marginal evidence to decide whether to add, remove, replace, or restore predictors.

children.name: Measure a candidate in isolation
children.description: Evaluate a candidate alone with its correct inference pipeline before interpreting its blend contribution.

children.name: Test one additional member
children.description: Add a candidate to the unchanged baseline and retain it only if its marginal contribution is supported.

children.name: Remove a harmful or redundant member
children.description: Perform controlled leave-one-out or subset ablations and retain the smaller pool when it improves held-out performance.

children.name: Replace one fixed ensemble slot
children.description: Swap one component checkpoint or model while holding other members and blend settings fixed.

children.name: Restore complementary members
children.description: Reassemble previously beneficial predictors after an isolation test or excessive pruning.

children.name: Retest membership after upstream changes
children.description: Re-evaluate prior inclusions and exclusions when other components or aggregation rules change.

children.name: Select a trained artifact
children.decision: Which checkpoint comparison should I perform?
children.description: Choose checkpoint candidates according to available training runs, stages, and validation evidence.

children.name: Compare trained runs or folds
children.description: Evaluate candidate checkpoint artifacts one at a time under a fixed compatible inference pipeline.

children.name: Compare training stages or stopping rules
children.description: Compare final, best-validation, clean-subset, or multi-stage snapshots rather than assuming the latest is best.

children.name: Compare full-data and fold-trained weights
children.description: Compare full-data, fold-only, and mixed checkpoint pools using independent evaluation.

children.name: Change prediction combination or output mapping
children.decision: Which operation on valid predictions should I change?
children.description: Choose a blend or post-processing intervention that matches the task metric and prediction semantics.

children.name: Choose a combination rule
children.decision: Which rule should I compare against the current aggregation?
children.description: Select an aggregation trial based on score scales, calibration, and available out-of-fold training data.

children.name: Compare rank and raw-score averaging
children.description: Test per-model rank normalization against raw averaging under the current ranking metric and model configuration.

children.name: Compare probability and logit aggregation
children.description: Compare averaging normalized probabilities with averaging logits followed by the required output activation.

children.name: Group before averaging
children.description: Average homogeneous folds or model families first, then combine groups to control their effective contribution.

children.name: Fit a regularized prediction stacker
children.description: Train a simple meta-learner on aligned out-of-fold predictions and compare it against direct averaging.

children.name: Change the meta-learner
children.description: Compare linear, kernel, Bayesian, or tree meta-learners with controlled regularization and held-out evaluation.

children.name: Try a nonlinear probability blend
children.description: Compare a power transform or power mean with arithmetic averaging on unchanged component predictions.

children.name: Choose how to weight predictors
children.decision: Which weighting strategy should I use as the next comparison?
children.description: Choose weight constraints and search scope according to evidence about component quality and validation stability.

children.name: Tune nonuniform blend weights
children.description: Optimize or sweep relative weights on fixed aligned predictions and compare with equal weighting.

children.name: Use a uniform-weight baseline
children.description: Restore or establish equal weights when quality differences or tuned-weight gains are not reliable.

children.name: Allow signed blend coefficients
children.description: Test negative coefficients when correlated errors may benefit from subtraction and the output semantics permit it.

children.name: Compare conditional and global weights
children.description: Test per-class or sample-dependent weighting against a fixed global blend.

children.name: Retune after component changes
children.description: Re-optimize weights after changing model quality, member count, normalization, or augmentation.

children.name: Normalize component scales
children.description: Compare raw, standardized, or robustly scaled component predictions before fitting blend weights.

children.name: Choose meta-model inputs
children.decision: Which stacking feature change should I test?
children.description: Choose an input modification while preserving the out-of-fold training and test schema.

children.name: Generate valid out-of-fold meta-features
children.description: Build aligned held-out base predictions with shared fold indices before fitting a downstream learner.

children.name: Add auxiliary stacking features
children.description: Test extra base outputs, embeddings, or auxiliary head predictions and retrain the meta-learner on the expanded schema.

children.name: Select a smaller meta-feature set
children.description: Compare curated subsets of base predictions or auxiliary features against the full stack.

children.name: Map continuous scores to discrete labels
children.decision: Which discretization rule should I compare?
children.description: Choose a mapping compatible with the target levels, metric, and calibration sample.

children.name: Optimize ordinal cutpoints
children.description: Fit ordered cutpoints on held-out predictions, retuning them after model changes.

children.name: Use simple clip-and-round
children.description: Compare simple rounding and clipping against learned cutpoints to detect calibration overfitting.

children.name: Match empirical target frequencies
children.description: Compare quantile or distribution-based label mapping with per-example thresholding.

children.name: Merge or threshold near-equal scores
children.description: Test per-target binning or thresholding for quasi-discrete labels with explicit tie handling.

children.name: Compare group-specific cutpoints
children.description: Use observable or independently predicted subgroups to compare separate calibration with a global mapping.

children.name: Handle degenerate bins and ties
children.description: Check constant output columns and tie behavior, restoring continuous outputs where binning destroys useful order.

children.name: Correct output semantics or bias
children.decision: Which output correction should I test or repair?
children.description: Distinguish invalid output conventions from residual bias in otherwise valid predictions.

children.name: Restore prediction units and activation
children.description: Apply the correct inverse target scaling, sigmoid, softmax, label offset, or probability normalization.

children.name: Align risk-score direction
children.description: Check whether larger scores mean greater risk and reverse inconsistent component signs before blending.

children.name: Rescale probabilities or logits
children.description: Compare temperature or per-class scaling with unmodified probabilities and renormalize as required.

children.name: Correct systematic prediction bias
children.description: Test a held-out mean shift, reference-example correction, or small additive offset.

children.name: Apply auxiliary or metadata corrections
children.description: Test confidence-gated classifier or high-precision metadata corrections on the relevant output subset.

children.name: Ablate an existing output transform
children.description: Toggle the current post-processing step without changing the model to verify it still helps.

children.name: Choose inference-time averaging
children.decision: Which repeated-view inference strategy should I test?
children.description: Select only transformations compatible with the task and evaluate their incremental contribution.

children.name: Average deterministic symmetry views
children.description: Compare original predictions with fixed flips or domain-specific channel symmetries.

children.name: Average windows or resolutions
children.description: Average predictions across valid temporal crops or spatial resolutions.

children.name: Compare stochastic forward-pass averaging
children.description: Test random transformations or active-dropout averaging against deterministic inference.

children.name: Disable unintended stochastic inference
children.description: Use evaluation mode and controlled randomness, checking whether repeated passes actually differ.

children.name: Make useful experiments feasible
children.decision: Which execution change removes the current bottleneck?
children.description: Choose a resource or engineering intervention that enables valid evaluation or full-strength inference.

children.name: Control peak resource use
children.decision: Which resource intervention fits the observed bottleneck?
children.description: Use measured memory or throughput behavior to choose a concrete implementation change.

children.name: Stream complete entities or prediction batches
children.description: Partition large data by safe boundaries and concatenate validated predictions without loading everything at once.

children.name: Release sequential model state
children.description: Free models and intermediate arrays after their last use before loading the next component.

children.name: Reduce stored feature precision
children.description: Downcast intermediate feature matrices where their ranges and precision permit it.

children.name: Tune inference batch size
children.description: Reduce batches to resolve memory failures or increase them for throughput while checking output invariance.

children.name: Compare inference precision
children.description: Test half or mixed precision against full precision with unchanged model and inputs.

children.name: Optimize expensive computation
children.description: Replace bottleneck operations with verified vectorized, compiled, or suitable backend implementations.

children.name: Shorten experiment turnaround
children.decision: What can I reduce or reuse without invalidating the experiment?
children.description: Choose between cheaper trial execution and reusing unchanged computation.

children.name: Run a reduced end-to-end smoke test
children.description: Use a small data slice, fold count, or training budget to verify correctness before a full run.

children.name: Cache expensive reusable artifacts
children.description: Persist features, embeddings, predictions, or fitted preprocessing so downstream trials reuse unchanged work.

children.name: Resume only unfinished training
children.description: Save fold or stage artifacts and run only missing work across sessions.

children.name: Restore full production execution
children.description: Verify debug guards, fold limits, and training shortcuts are disabled when generating the final evaluated prediction.

children.name: Make pipeline changes reproducible
children.decision: Which code-organization change addresses the observed fragility?
children.description: Choose an explicit reproducibility intervention and verify it preserves intended outputs.

children.name: Parameterize and separate model pipelines
children.description: Use explicit configurations and reusable or model-specific inference components to prevent integration drift.

children.name: Verify a cleanup or inference-only refactor
children.description: Remove obsolete code incrementally and compare predictions with a saved reference.

children.name: Pin configurations and artifacts
children.description: Record exact settings, checkpoint manifests, seeds, and selected weights to reproduce a result.

children.name: Make missing-component behavior explicit
children.description: Detect missing prediction artifacts and validate any fallback or reduced ensemble rather than silently emitting placeholders.
